Sodium chlorate (NaClO3) is a chemical compound with the following properties:

A. It can explode in the presence of coal or sulfur - This is true. Sodium chlorate is a strong oxidizing agent that can react violently with reducing agents like coal or sulfur, potentially causing explosions.

B. It is a salt of chloric acid - This is true. Sodium chlorate is formed from the neutralization of chloric acid (HClO3) with sodium hydroxide (NaOH) or sodium carbonate (Na2CO3).

C. It is not approved as a weedkiller - This is false. Sodium chlorate has been used as a herbicide/weedkiller, although its use is restricted in some regions due to safety concerns.

D. It may only be stored in paper bags - This is false. Due to its oxidizing properties, sodium chlorate should be stored in appropriate containers away from combustible materials, not in paper bags which would be a safety hazard.

Based on my analysis, option B is correct as sodium chlorate is indeed a salt of chloric acid (HClO3).
